issues.claim: Round 6 (R6-10, VAT-r5-02) gave a public note in a picture its form: §11.2's `ExportOpts.pins` (base l. 16323–16329) 'each public note a numbered marker at its thing's anchor … numbered from 1 … the numbers keyed on §9.5's separate legend sheet to the pin's label and note and to the public note's text; a public note on a thing the export's knowledge withholds left out', and §9.5 (l. 15168–15169) adds the public notes to its *Annotation layer* ('numbered markers and a separate legend sheet'); the canon's round-6 ruling says the same. A note's words now reach a picture only on the legend sheet. V08's players' view still promises the players the notes: §3.14 (2) (l. 2299–2301) 'Every picture is drawn with … the document's public notes, view pins and annotation layer (§2.9 view state, §9.5)'; §5.3's *Notes and pins in pictures* (l. 3110–3113) 'the players see the public ones in their pictures'; T-V8-41 (l. 3308) 'public notes and view pins are drawn, private ones never'. The set has no carrier for the sheet: `PartyPictureSet` (l. 377–383) holds `levels` (PNG tiles), `svg` and `gazetteer`, `drawDigest` hashes those alone, `putPartyPictures` stores only that, the player's viewer (§3.14 (4), l. 2319–2322) shows the tiles and a caption, and the party gazetteer holds places, not notes. A player gets numbered markers with no text. Two builders differ: one invents a legend member the record, the digest and the viewer lack; one draws the note text on the tiles against §11.2; one leaves the notes out against V08 §5.3 and T-V8-41. §5.3's bullet also says every picture draws the notes, where §11.2 draws them 'never in a picture unless asked' (`pins` default false), and it does not say that a party render always asks. The subject is shared by rendering (§9.5, §11.2), V08 (the party set, `exportPicture`) and V09 (the Picture tab's 'pins and public notes'); the agreement matrix has no row for it.
issues.required_change: V08. (1) `PartyPictureSet` (l. 381), after `gazetteer: Uint8Array /* … */;` add `legend: Uint8Array /* §9.5's legend sheet of the set's annotation layer — each numbered view pin's label and note and each numbered public note's text, numbered as §11.2's ExportOpts.pins numbers the markers on the tiles and the SVG — under the party key, an SVG inert by §11.1's bar; an empty sheet when the set draws no marker */;` and in `drawDigest`'s comment 'the gazetteer's bytes and `week`' → 'the gazetteer's and the legend's bytes and `week`'. (2) §3.14 (2), the closing clause: 'the document's public notes, view pins and annotation layer (§2.9 view state, §9.5) and never a private note or a DM-only pin.' → 'the document's view pins and public notes as §9.5's annotation layer — every party render passes `ExportOpts.pins` true, so each is a numbered marker on the tiles and the SVG, a note on a place the party key withholds left out (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`), keyed on the set's legend sheet (`legend`, drawn by the same render) — and never a private note or a DM-only pin.' (3) §3.14 (4): after 'the caption `host.party.asOf` (the set's `week`; V08 §5.1's table)' add ', the set's legend sheet (`legend`) below the tiles when it keys any marker'. (4) §5.3's *Notes and pins in pictures*: 'A picture draws the document's public notes and view pins and the annotation layer (§2.9 view state, §9.5) under its key;' → 'A picture draws the document's view pins and public notes as §9.5's annotation layer — numbered markers keyed on its legend sheet — when its `ExportOpts.pins` asks (§11.2; every party render asks, V08 §3.14 (2)), under its key, a note on a thing the key withholds left out;'. (5) T-V8-41: 'public notes and view pins are drawn, private ones never' → 'public notes and view pins are drawn as numbered markers keyed on the set's legend sheet (`legend`), a public note on a place the party key withholds left out, private ones never'. One fix with VAH-r6-02.

issues.claim: V08 §3.14 (5) (l. 2326–2331) says of 'See what the players see': 'So the DM sees in the live frame exactly what the next party set will show'. T-V8-41 (l. 3308) asserts it: 'with "See what the players see" on, the frame's city band equals the party set's z0 picture at the same head (a pixel diff, both drawn with the fixed sun)'. Since round 6 the two cannot be equal on any document holding a view pin or a public note. The party set draws each view pin as 'a numbered marker in its colour at its point' and each public note as 'a numbered marker at its thing's anchor' (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`, base l. 16323–16329; §9.5 l. 15168). The live frame draws 'pins as markers with their colour; notes in panels' (V09's entity table, l. 4171; §4.19's Notes and Pins rows, l. 2907–2908): unnumbered pins and no note marker. T-V8-41's own fixture holds both (the same bar asserts 'public notes and view pins are drawn'), so its pixel diff cannot pass as written. Two builders differ: one draws the annotation layer in the frame while the toggle is on (a canvas mode V09 does not define), one runs the diff only on a fixture with no pin or note. Before round 6, §11.2 drew pins 'as the view draws them', so the frame and the set could agree.
issues.required_change: V08. (1) §3.14 (5): 'So the DM sees in the live frame exactly what the next party set will show;' → 'So the DM sees in the live frame exactly what the next party set will show but its annotation layer — the view pins and public notes the set draws as numbered markers keyed on its legend sheet (§11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`), which the frame shows as V09 §4.19 does —;'. (2) T-V8-41: 'the frame's city band equals the party set's z0 picture at the same head (a pixel diff, both drawn with the fixed sun)' → 'the frame's city band equals the party set's z0 picture at the same head (a pixel diff, both drawn with the fixed sun, on the fixture's copy holding no view pin and no public note — the set's numbered markers being the annotation layer the frame does not draw, §11.2's `ExportOpts.pins`)'. One fix with VAH-r6-01.

issues.claim: R6-03's residue in the base's one statement of the port. §7.7 item 1 (base l. 11946–11950): 'the port DIFFS the incoming dossier against the dossier facts the map already carries … writes one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13), dates it by §4.11's dating rungs (item 76) and emits its events'; §14 port item 4 (l. 19919–19920) says 'into one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13)'. Since round 6, an absorb whose week is not after the last epoch's writes no change for three things it finds changed: a late calamity, its F5 targets' records and a condition naming it. Their carried facts stay as they were, and the next absorb past that week carries them (§4.11 *The clock* (4), l. 8531; V08 §3.6 (3), (4), l. 1873–1876, 1927–1928; V08 §3.2, l. 1530–1531). R6-01 (2) (d) puts the base's summaries in each ruling's sweep. R6-03's sweep searched §7.7 item 10 and §14's port comments for a held list, but not item 1's 'one per changed element'. Read alone, item 1 writes a `DossierChange` for each of the three, and the ledger fold (`carried[key] = after`) would then carry them. A port builder follows §4.11 (4) and V08 §3.6 (3), which item 1 cites by '§4.11', so nothing built changes. §14 item 4's 'groups them by §4.11's cadence' carries the exception by citation; its 'one per changed element' does not.
issues.required_change: Determinism, §7.7 item 1: 'writes one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13), dates it by §4.11's dating rungs (item 76)' → 'writes one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13) — none, in an absorb whose week is not after the last epoch's, for a late calamity, its F5 targets' records and a condition naming it, which the next absorb past that week carries (§4.11 *The clock* (4)) — dates it by §4.11's dating rungs (item 76)'. Second end, scope: §14 port item 4, 'into one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13)' → 'into one `DossierChange` per changed element (§7.7 item 13; none for what §4.11 *The clock* (4) leaves uncarried)'.
